title: Integer endpoint discontinuity of normalized uniformization for positively curved surfaces
original_description:
For every fixed nonnegative finite integer r, we construct smooth complete metrics of strictly positive Gaussian curvature on both the plane and sphere that converge in ordinary compact-open C^r, while their unique point-normalized uniformizing diffeomorphisms fail compact-open C^(r+1) convergence. The critical r=1 case uses a small C^1 conformal correction controlling the full nonlinear inverse-coordinate curvature operator. This resolves the specified finite-integer endpoint question recorded in the 2017 Oberwolfach report, published on 3 January 2018.

The theorem concerns this specific normalized parametrization of smooth objects and makes no assertion about abstract homeomorphisms, RP^2, smooth or noninteger Holder topologies. Classical logarithmic and twisting mechanisms are credited. A bounded primary-source search through 3 October 2026 did not locate an earlier full geometric resolution, with residual risk of an earlier unindexed realization; exhaustive historical priority is not claimed. The compact support package supplies standalone manuscript source and standard-library exact finite diagnostics. Finite checks supplement the universal proof and do not certify all orders, global curvature, completeness or novelty.

AI tools were used extensively in construction, derivation, drafting, adversarial review and verification. This version 1.0 preprint is unrefereed; no human peer review, journal acceptance or formal proof certification is claimed. The manuscript and new documentation are CC BY 4.0; Python code is MIT.
